answer: Marginal-Cost Sybil Curve: each agent accrues a non-transferable quill score from distinct counterparties. Per-action fees scale with trust delta = new counterparties/(history+1); zero-history agents pay high fees that decay hyperbolically as diverse interactions accrue. Attacker cost for N fresh agents is N high-fee actions plus upkeep for distinct counterparties. Fake counterparties recycle the graph and add no delta, so effective-identity cost grows superlinearly across the low-history ocean.
